text:
alex: seeing a rash of RX/TX errors and VF resets on g6gn fleet since the 6.4 kernel roll yesterday. net stats spike and some nodes show east-west packet loss to pod CIDR ranges

maria: same cluster here (us-west-2, gpu-pool-3). errors start ~10m after boot. dmesg shows repeated i40e VF reset messages

kyle: can you paste dmesg snip? are these SR-IOV VFs or regular PFs? we use SR-IOV for gpu nodes right now

alex: SR-IOV VFs. snippet: ```
[ 1234.567890] i40e 0000:81:00.1: VF 3 reset (reason 0x6)
[ 1234.568012] i40e 0000:81:00.1: VF 7 reset (reason 0x6)
[ 1234.570001] i40e 0000:81:00.1: PF link state changed to 0
```

maria: we also see `rx_errors` bumping on eth0 and GSO segmentation errors in tcpdump when pod-to-pod traffic goes across host. sample tcpdump: ```
14:22:30.123456 IP 10.2.1.5 > 10.2.2.7: UDP, bad checksum, length 1400
14:22:30.123457 IP 10.2.1.5 > 10.2.2.7: IP csum failed, segmented packet
```

alex: rolling kernel back to 6.3 on one node stopped the flaps. also tried disabling GRO/GSO with `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off` and that temporarily stabilized RX drops

kyle: interesting. did you notice any MTU mismatches? we have Geneve overlay MTU 1450 on some nodes, might interact with offloads

maria: MTU is 1450 everywhere in that pool. I flushed offloads + reduced MTU to 1400 on one canary, packets stopped fragmenting but VF resets still occured a few mins later

alex: opened AWS support case and vendor (Intel) ticket. AWS says driver/firmware combo with i40e in this hw revision is flaky with SR-IOV active after recent kernel changes

sre-bot: incident-created: INC-2026-0423-11 - inter-host packet loss on g6gn-gpu-pool-3 (assigned: kyle)

kyle: plan: 1) drain affected AZ nodes 2) set sriov_numvfs=0 on kernel cmdline for a quick rollback 3) schedule firmware downgrade for NICs if vendor confirms 4) revert kernel roll in control plane if correlation holds

tony: note re: cost/ops impact — draining ~120 g6gn nodes will push some jobs to on-demand and bump GPU spend ~18% for 24h. need approval if we do broad drain

maria: for now I'll patch node-config to disable SR-IOV on new boots in pool and add kube-affinity to avoid rescheduling critical workloads to canaries

alex: logs/links I've added to the ticket: `dmesg +ethtool -S +/var/log/pods/tcpdump.pcap` on three nodes, kernel module versions, and our kernel rollback test results

kyle: thanks. i'll coordinate with infra on the controlled drain and get procurement signoff if we need extra reserved capacity for burst. will update INC-2026-0423-11

maria: quick workaround (if anyone needs it): run on node: `sudo modprobe -r i40e && sudo modprobe i40e max_vfs=0` then restart kubelet. not ideal but buys time

alex: marking nodes with label `nic-unstable=true` so autoscaler won't touch them until we finish work :thumbsup:

sre-bot: incident-updated: INC-2026-0423-11 - mitigation applied: SR-IOV disabled on new boots, canary drain scheduled

kyle: final ask: please keep packet captures and ethtool stats for affected nodes for 72h. intel contact requested NIC firmware dump too.

maria: copied. i'll attach pcaps to the intel ticket and tag you all.

alex: thanks all, will post postmortem after root cause confirmed
